Below is a 3‑week reconditioning block designed to safely restore capacity, rebuild tolerance to volume and intensity, and guide the client back toward pre-illness performance. It uses conservative loading, slightly higher frequency for main lifts, submaximal RPE targets, and built-in recovery. The aim is to finish Week 3 ready to transition into normal training loads/periodization.

Context and guiding principles
- Training frequency: 4 days/week (Upper/Lower split with one full-body strength day and one lighter GPP/conditioning day).
- Intensity: Start at 60–70% of pre-illness estimated 1RM and progress to 75–85% by end of Week 3, guided by RPE and daily readiness.
- RPE caps: Keep main lifts mostly at RPE 6–7 in Weeks 1–2; touch RPE 7–8 in Week 3 on top sets, with back-off volume at RPE 6–7.
- Volume: Moderate total sets, emphasizing quality reps, long enough rest (2–4 min compounds, 60–90s assistance).
- Auto-regulation: If persistent fatigue is present on a given day, reduce top set load by 2.5–5% or cut one back-off set.
- Conditioning: Low to moderate intensity, strictly nasal or conversational pace early on; progress duration slightly each week.
- Mobility/Prehab: Daily brief practice for shoulders/hips/ankles; incorporate light breathing work post-session.
- Sleep/Recovery: Prioritize 7.5–9 hours sleep; step count target 7–10k/day unless excessively fatigued.

Estimated training maxes for loading reference (pre-illness 1RMs)
- Bench 100 kg, Squat 140 kg, Deadlift 170 kg.
- Week 1 loads around 60–70% of these; Week 2: 65–75%; Week 3: 70–85% with only brief exposures to the top end.

Week 1 — Reload and Movement Quality
Goal: Restore movement patterns and tolerance; keep all work submaximal (RPE 6–7), longer rest, crisp technique, leave 3–4 reps in reserve.

Day 1 (Lower Focus)
- Back Squat: 4 sets x 5 reps @ ~60–65% (84–91 kg), RPE 6.
- Romanian Deadlift (barbell or DB): 3 x 8 @ RPE 6.
- Split Squat (rear foot elevated optional): 3 x 8/side @ RPE 6.
- Plank: 3 x 45–60s.
- Easy Bike or Walk: 10–12 min conversational pace.

Day 2 (Upper Push + Pull)
- Bench Press: 4 x 5 @ ~60–65% (60–65 kg), RPE 6.
- One-Arm DB Row: 3 x 10/side @ RPE 6.
- Incline DB Bench: 3 x 10 @ RPE 6.
- Lat Pulldown or Pull-Up (assisted if needed): 3 x 8–10 @ RPE 6.
- Face Pulls or Band Y/T/W: 2–3 x 12–15.
- Easy Erg or Walk: 10–12 min.

Day 3 (Full-Body Strength, Light)
- Deadlift (conventional): 3 x 4 @ ~60–65% (102–111 kg), RPE 6.
- Front Squat or Goblet Squat: 3 x 6 @ RPE 6.
- Overhead Press (barbell or DB): 3 x 6 @ RPE 6.
- Hip Airplanes or Single-Leg RDL (bodyweight/DB): 2–3 x 8/side.
- Core: Pallof Press 3 x 10/side.

Day 4 (GPP/Conditioning + Accessories)
- Conditioning: 20–25 min steady state at easy pace (RPE 3–4). Options: incline walk, bike, rower. Nasal breathing.
- Accessory circuit (2–3 rounds, easy pace): 
  - Hamstring curl 12
  - Cable fly 12
  - Seated cable row 12
  - Copenhagen plank 20–30s/side
- Mobility: 8–10 minutes hips/shoulders/ankles, diaphragmatic breathing 3–5 min.

Notes Week 1
- If session RPE feels >7 or fatigue lingers, cut last set of main lift.
- Keep bar speed snappy; terminate a set if reps slow markedly.

Week 2 — Build Volume and Slight Intensity Bump
Goal: Nudge intensity and volume; introduce a single slightly heavier top set at RPE 7, back-offs at RPE 6–7. Conditioning increases modestly.

Day 1 (Lower Focus)
- Back Squat: Top set 1 x 4 @ ~70% (98 kg) RPE ~7; then 3 x 5 @ 65% (91 kg) RPE 6–7.
- RDL: 3 x 8 @ RPE 6–7 (slightly heavier than W1).
- Walking Lunge: 3 x 10/leg @ RPE 6–7.
- Hanging Knee Raise: 3 x 10–12.
- Bike/Row: 12–15 min easy.

Day 2 (Upper Push + Pull)
- Bench Press: Top set 1 x 4 @ ~70% (70 kg) RPE ~7; then 3 x 5 @ 65% (65 kg) RPE 6–7.
- Chest-Supported Row: 3 x 8–10 @ RPE 7.
- Incline DB Bench: 3 x 8–10 @ RPE 7.
- Lat Pulldown or Pull-Up: 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 7.
- Rear Delt Raise + Band External Rotation: 2–3 x 12–15 each.

Day 3 (Full-Body Strength, Moderate)
- Deadlift: Top set 1 x 3 @ ~70% (119 kg) RPE ~7; then 3 x 3–4 @ 65% (111 kg) RPE 6–7.
- Front Squat: 3 x 5 @ RPE 6–7 (light–moderate).
- Overhead Press: 3 x 5 @ RPE 6–7.
- Single-Leg RDL: 2–3 x 8/side @ RPE 6–7.
- Core: Side Plank 3 x 30–45s/side.

Day 4 (GPP/Conditioning + Accessories)
- Conditioning: 25–30 min steady state, RPE 3–4.
- Accessory circuit (2–3 rounds):
  - Leg press 12 @ RPE 6–7
  - Cable row 12
  - Cable lateral raise 12–15
  - Farmer Carry 4 x 30–40 m moderate

Notes Week 2
- If any top set feels like RPE 8, stay there and keep back-offs the same or reduce one set.
- Maintain rest 2–3 min compounds, 60–90s accessories.

Week 3 — Readiness Check and Return-to-Baseline Prep
Goal: Brief exposures to higher intensity (RPE 7–8) on main lifts with low volume; confirm tolerance and bar speed. Finish feeling fresher, not trashed.

Day 1 (Lower Focus — Squat Emphasis)
- Back Squat: 
  - Warm-up to Top set 1 x 3 @ ~75–80% (105–112 kg) RPE 7–8.
  - Back-off 2–3 x 4 @ 70% (98 kg) RPE 6–7.
- RDL: 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 7.
- Split Squat: 2 x 8/side @ RPE 7.
- Core: Ab wheel 3 x 8–10.
- Easy cardio: 10 min.

Day 2 (Upper — Bench Emphasis)
- Bench Press:
  - Top set 1 x 3 @ ~75–80% (75–80 kg) RPE 7–8.
  - Back-off 2–3 x 4 @ 70% (70 kg) RPE 6–7.
- Row (chest-supported or cable): 3 x 8 @ RPE 7.
- Incline DB Bench: 2–3 x 8 @ RPE 7.
- Pull-Ups or Pulldown: 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 7.
- Scap/rotator cuff: Face pulls 2 x 15; Cable ER 2 x 12.

Day 3 (Full-Body — Deadlift Emphasis)
- Deadlift:
  - Top set 1 x 2–3 @ ~77–82% (131–139 kg) RPE 7–8.
  - Back-off 2–3 x 3 @ 70% (119 kg) RPE 6–7.
- Front Squat or Pause Squat (2s): 3 x 3–4 @ RPE 6–7.
- Overhead Press: 3 x 4–6 @ RPE 6–7.
- Single-Leg hinge/hip airplane: 2 x 6–8/side.
- Core: Pallof ISO hold 3 x 20–30s/side.

Day 4 (GPP/Conditioning + Potentiation)
- Conditioning: 25–30 min at RPE 3–4. Optional 4–6 x 10s strides/spin-ups with 90s easy between to reintroduce brief higher outputs (stop if HRV/readiness is down).
- Light accessories (2 rounds only, leave fresh):
  - Leg curl 12
  - Cable row 12
  - DB lateral raise 15
  - Farmer carry 3 x 30 m light–moderate
- Mobility/breathing: 10 min.

End-of-Week 3 Readiness Markers
- No excessive DOMS or lingering fatigue >24–36h.
- Can hit top sets at RPE 7–8 with stable bar speed.
- Resting HR and sleep back to baseline; appetite normalized.

Recovery, Fatigue Management, and Monitoring
- Warm-up template (each session):
  - 3–5 min easy cardio + breathing (4s in through nose, 6s out).
  - 1–2 mobility drills each: ankles, hips, T-spine, shoulders (total 5–7 min).
  - 2–3 ramp-up sets per main lift with gradual load jumps.
- Cooldown:
  - 3–5 min easy bike/walk + 2–3 minutes nasal breathing, long exhales.
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours; consistent schedule.
- Hydration: 35–45 ml/kg/day; add 500–1000 ml around training.
- Illness recovery watch-outs: If morning HR is >10% above baseline for 2+ days, or fatigue >24–48h after sessions, reduce next session volume by 20–30% and keep intensity ≤RPE 6.

Nutrition (to support weight regain and recovery)
- Calorie target: Aim for ~200–300 kcal/day surplus above current maintenance to regain 4 kg gradually over 6–10 weeks; for first 3 weeks, ensure at least maintenance if appetite is low.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, distribute across 3–5 meals; include 25–40 g high-quality protein within 1–2 hours post-training.
- Carbohydrate: 3–5 g/kg/day; ensure 1–1.5 g/kg in the 24h after training days to support glycogen restoration.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; include omega-3s (1–2 g EPA/DHA daily).
- Micronutrients: Vitamin D (1000–2000 IU/day if low), a basic multi, and electrolytes (sodium 2–3 g/day added as needed if sweating).
- Appetite strategies: Liquid calories (milk/yogurt smoothies), easy carbs around training, salt food for palatability.

Progression and transition
- If Week 3 top sets felt ≤RPE 7 with solid bar speed, you can estimate readiness to resume ~80–85% work in the first mesocycle back, using conservative training maxes (e.g., bench 95, squat 135, deadlift 165) and build from there.
- If any lift still feels lagging, keep that lift one week behind (repeat Week 3 pattern) while progressing others.

Safety and form cues
- Keep reps fast and stop 1–3 reps before any technical breakdown.
- Use belts/wrist wraps as previously tolerated; avoid grinding reps during this block.
- Emphasize full ROM, neutral spine, active bracing, and consistent bar paths.

Guardrails and modifications
- If any musculoskeletal niggle or HR is unusually high for pace, cut the run short and replace next run with bike/row at the same duration.
- If DOMS is heavy after squats/deads, push Run A back 24 hours or drop it by 10–15 min.
- Shoes: rotate a cushioned pair for easy runs; avoid aggressive tempos for this block.

Fueling around runs
- Easy runs <45 min: water + optional small carb snack if lifting after.
- Longer run (Week 3 50–60 min): 20–30 g carbs 30–60 min pre-run; top up fluids and sodium, eat a normal carb/protein meal after.

By the end of Week 3 he should comfortably cover the 10k duration at easy effort, with legs feeling responsive for lifting. Transition in Week 4 to maintaining a weekly 10k easy run plus one shorter aerobic run or a light progression (e.g., add gentle fartlek only if recovery is solid).

Here’s a practical 3-week reconditioning nutrition plan to support recovery, performance, and gradual weight regain. Assumes a 41-year-old intermediate male lifter who lost ~4 kg after illness.

Primary goals
- Restore energy availability to eliminate persistent fatigue.
- Regain 0.25–0.5 kg per week initially (first 3–6 weeks), then taper to 0.2–0.3 kg/week.
- Support training quality (lifting + return to 10k) with sufficient carbs and protein.

Calorie targets
- Find current maintenance: With reduced body mass and activity returning, a quick start point is 32–34 kcal/kg body weight on training days and 28–30 kcal/kg on rest days, then adjust by the scale.
- For weight regain: Add 200–350 kcal/day above current maintenance.
- If you prefer a single number: 34–36 kcal/kg on training days; 30–32 kcal/kg on rest days.
- Rate check: Aim for +0.25–0.5 kg/week. If <0.25 kg/week after 7–10 days, add 150–200 kcal/day; if >0.6 kg/week for 2 straight weeks, pull 150–200 kcal/day.

Macros (by body weight; adjust to his current weight)
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day. Distribute over 3–5 meals with 25–40 g per meal. Include 30–40 g within 1–2 hours post-lift.
- Carbohydrate: 4–6 g/kg/day on lifting + running days; 3–5 g/kg/day on rest/GPP days.
  - Pre-lift/run: 30–60 g carbs 60–120 min prior (easily digested).
  - Post: 1–1.5 g/kg carbs over the 24 h after harder days.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Keep at least 20–25% of total calories from fat for hormones and satiety.

Hydration and electrolytes
- Fluids: 35–45 ml/kg/day baseline. Add 500–750 ml around each training hour.
- Sodium: 2–3 g/day added sodium (total dietary sodium often 3–5 g) especially on run days or if sweat rate is high.
- Carb + sodium combo during the Week 3 long run (50–60 min): optional 15–30 g carbs + 300–500 mg sodium if heat/humidity is high.

Micronutrients and supplements
- Omega-3s: 1–2 g/day combined EPA+DHA.
- Vitamin D3: 1000–2000 IU/day if blood levels unknown/low.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, daily, no cycling; supports strength recovery.
- Whey or milk protein: convenient to hit targets.
- A simple multi/mineral if diet variety is low.
- Probiotics or fermented foods if appetite/GI was impacted post-illness.

Meal timing framework
- 3–5 meals/day. Bookend training with carbs + protein.
- Example timing on lift+run day:
  - Breakfast: Protein 30–40 g + 60–90 g carbs + some fruit.
  - Pre-training snack (60–120 min out): 30–50 g carbs + 10–25 g protein.
  - Post-training meal (within 2 h): 30–40 g protein + 80–120 g carbs, low–moderate fat.
  - Evening meal: protein + starch + veg + fats to round daily targets.

If you want concrete numbers, plug in his current body weight
- Example using 80 kg current weight (adjust if different):
  - Training days: 34–36 kcal/kg → 2720–2880 kcal; target a small surplus ~2950–3100 kcal.
  - Rest days: 30–32 kcal/kg → 2400–2560 kcal; target ~2600–2750 kcal.
  - Protein: 150–175 g/day.
  - Carbs: 320–480 g/day (lower end on rest/GPP days, higher on squat/deadlift + run days).
  - Fat: 65–80 g/day.

Appetite and GI-friendly strategies
- Liquid nutrition: milk or yogurt smoothies with whey, oats, banana, honey.
- Easy-to-eat carbs: rice, pasta, potatoes, oats, breads, fruit, juices.
- Add fats for calorie density if appetite is low: olive oil, nut butters, avocado.
- Salt food to taste; include broths on high-sweat days.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Track body weight 3–4 mornings/week, fasted. Look for weekly average change.
- If fatigue persists or training quality dips, first increase carbs by 50–100 g/day before pushing fat up.
- Reassess every 7–10 days; adjust calories by 150–200 kcal as needed.
- Sleep 7.5–9 h and keep steps moderate (7–10k/day) to channel resources into recovery.

This approach restores energy availability, supports performance, and regains weight at a sustainable pace while minimizing GI stress after illness.

Short answer: not reasonable. Feeling normal today doesn’t mean his tissues, nervous system, and energy systems are ready for pre-illness loading. After 3 weeks off with weight loss and persistent fatigue, the risks of jumping straight back to baseline loads (loss of tolerance, higher RPE at old percentages, form breakdown) outweigh any small time savings.

Key considerations
- Deconditioning window: Even in trained lifters, strength expression drops 3–10% after 2–3 weeks off, and work capacity drops faster than peak strength. He’s also 4 kg lighter, so prior absolute loads will likely carry a higher relative intensity now.
- Illness aftermath: Flu-related inflammation, altered hydration, and disrupted sleep/appetite blunt recovery. Readiness can feel normal at rest but degrade quickly under load.
- Injury risk: Tendon and connective tissue tolerance lags behind “felt” energy. Most strains/pulls after time off come from reintroducing high intensity and volume too quickly.
- Performance psychology: One bad session grinding at old maxes can dent confidence more than a week of smooth submaximal work.

A rational compromise if he’s adamant
- Keep Week 1 structure but allow a slightly higher top exposure on each main lift while keeping overall volume controlled. Use RPE caps and bar speed to decide load, not ego.
- Targets for first exposures this week:
  - Squat: Work up to 1 top set of 4 at RPE 7 (~70–72.5% of old 1RM: 98–102.5 kg), then 2–3 x 4–5 at ~65–68% (91–95 kg).
  - Bench: Top set 1 x 4 at RPE 7 (~70%: 70 kg), then 2–3 x 4–5 at 65–68% (65–68 kg).
  - Deadlift: Top set 1 x 3 at RPE 7 (~70–72.5%: 119–123 kg), then 2–3 x 3 at 65–68% (111–116 kg).
- If those top sets feel like RPE ≤6 with crisp bar speed, add 2.5–5 kg the next session—don’t jump straight to pre-illness loads in the same day.
- Keep accessories at RPE 6–7 and cut one set if fatigue creeps.
- Running: Hold the Week 1 easy durations; don’t combine heavier deadlifts with a long run within 24 hours.

Red flags to abort and regress
- Morning HR >10% above baseline for 2+ days.
- Session RPE >8 on what should be submaximal work, or obvious bar speed drop.
- DOMS >48 h or joint/tendon irritation.

What “starting at old loads” would look like and why to avoid it this week
- Pre-illness working sets likely sat around 75–85% on main lifts. Today, that could feel like 80–90% due to detraining and lower body mass. Grinding reps at RPE 9–10 in Week 1 raises risk and can stall week-2 progress.

Bottom line
- Give him one “readiness check” top set at RPE 7 on each main lift this week, then back-off work as planned. If all three lifts are snappy across sessions and recovery markers stay normal, we can fast-forward to the Week 3 template next week. Skipping straight to pre-illness loads today is unnecessary risk for minimal upside.

Here’s a clear checklist to greenlight full-intensity training (i.e., normal pre-illness loading, top sets RPE 8–9, normal weekly volume). Aim to see most or all of these for 7–10 consecutive days.

Performance signals (in-session)
- Top sets at RPE 7 feel genuinely submaximal:
  - Squat: 1 x 3–4 at ~75–80% moves fast with no sticking point.
  - Bench: 1 x 3–4 at ~75–80% smooth, stable scapular control.
  - Deadlift: 1 x 2–3 at ~77–82% with clean lockouts, no back rounding.
- Bar speed consistency: Velocity loss within a set ≤20% on main lifts (if using a VBT device) or subjective bar speed looks uniform across reps without grind.
- Stable technique under fatigue: Last reps of back-off sets look like first reps—no knee cave, no soft lockouts, no loss of brace.
- Volume tolerance: Can complete planned back-off work (8–12 total hard sets per session across compounds/assistance) without needing to cut sets due to fatigue.

Recovery signals (between sessions)
- DOMS minimal or resolves within 24–36 hours, even after squat/deadlift days.
- No joint/tendon irritability the morning after training.
- Sleep quality normal (fall asleep easily, minimal night wakings).
- Appetite normal to high; no nausea or GI turmoil after training days.

Physiological readiness
- Resting heart rate at or below pre-illness baseline for a week.
- HRV back to personal normal and stable (if tracked).
- RPE drift is low on easy runs: Week-3 50–60 min easy run feels truly easy; breathing remains nasal/conversational without pace drop.

Workload markers across a week
- Can handle two exposures per lift (e.g., bench twice, squat and deadlift once each or similar) without cumulative fatigue spilling into other sessions.
- No need for intra-week load reductions beyond normal day-to-day micro-adjustments (≤2.5 kg).
- Able to combine a lower-body strength day and an easy run within 24–36 hours without legs feeling “dead.”

Objective performance benchmarks (use any two or more)
- Hit a controlled single at ~85% on each main lift at RPE ≤7.5 with clean form.
- Complete 3 x 3 at ~80% on squat and deadlift and 3 x 4 at ~75–80% on bench with ≤2 min rep-to-rep bar-speed degradation and RPE ≤8.
- Rep PR proxies: 
  - Squat: 90–100 kg x 8 moves like RPE ≤7.
  - Bench: 70–75 kg x 8 at RPE ≤7.
  - Deadlift: 120–130 kg x 6 at RPE ≤7.
  (Adjust loads to his current state; these are proportional to ~65–70% ranges.)

Running-specific readiness
- Weekly 10k completed at easy effort with no next-day heaviness.
- Able to add 4–6 relaxed strides after an easy run without any calf/Achilles or hip niggles.

Decision rule to resume full intensity
- If ≥80% of the above boxes are ticked for 7–10 days AND the last week’s top sets felt like RPE ≤7.5 with crisp bar speed, move to normal programming:
  - Reintroduce top sets at RPE 8–9.
  - Restore usual weekly set volume over 1–2 weeks (e.g., add 2–4 total hard sets per lift).
  - Keep one “easy” day in the week for another week as a buffer.

If signals are mixed
- Keep intensity exposures (top sets at RPE 7–8) but hold volume steady another week.
- For any single lagging lift, progress the others while repeating the current week’s plan for that lift alone.

Red flags to delay full intensity
- Morning RHR >10% above baseline for 2+ days.
- Session RPEs unexpectedly >8 at sub-80% loads.
- DOMS or joint pain persisting >48 hours, or any tendon hot spots.
- Easy runs feel hard (breath rate high, pace drops noticeably at same RPE).

Use this as a simple traffic-light system: green when performance, recovery, and physiology align; yellow if one domain lags; red if two or more lagging signs appear.

Good idea—let’s add a controlled 1RM (or near-max) test late in Week 3 to anchor new training maxes without overshooting recovery. We’ll use a two-day test split with sensible warm-ups, velocity/RPE guardrails, and clear stop rules. If you don’t use VBT, rely on RPE and bar speed by eye.

Scheduling
- Day 3 (Fri or Sat): Deadlift + Squat test
- Day 2 (Wed/Thu): Bench test
- Day 4 GPP becomes recovery-only (easy spin/walk 15–20 min + mobility)

Rationale
- Bench gets its own day so upper body is fresh.
- Lower body tests are paired, but deadlift first while freshest; squat after a moderate top exposure (not full grind) to limit fatigue.

General test rules
- Cap at RPE 9 on any true max attempt this block (one rep in reserve). If you accidentally hit RPE 10 or technique breaks, terminate testing for that lift.
- Take 3–5 min rest between heavier singles.
- If a single is slower than prior warm-up by a clear margin or form wobbles, do not add load; either repeat or stop.
- Use fractional plates for small jumps (1–2.5 kg).

Bench test day (mid-Week 3)
1) Warm-up
- 5–7 min easy cardio + shoulder/pec T-spine prep.
- Bar x 8–10
- 40% x 5
- 55% x 3
- 65% x 2
- 72.5% x 1
- 80% x 1 (RPE ~6–7). If this single feels heavy (>RPE 7.5), stop at a conservative “daily max” around 82.5–85% and skip heavier attempts.

2) Test ladder
- 85% x 1
- 90% x 1 (assess RPE and bar speed)
- If RPE ≤8 and fast: 95% x 1
- Optional final attempt: 97.5–100% x 1 ONLY if the 95% rep was smooth, no grind, and spotter confirms speed.
- Otherwise, call the best fast single your “training max single.”

Example numbers from 100 kg pre-illness 1RM
- 80% 80 kg, 85% 85 kg, 90% 90 kg, 95% 95 kg, 97.5% 97.5 kg, 100% 100 kg
- Likely landing spot this block: 92.5–97.5 kg fast single.

Post-test back-off (optional)
- 2 x 2 @ ~85% if he wants some extra work and feels great; skip if any fatigue.

Deadlift + Squat test day (late-Week 3)
Order: Deadlift first, then Squat.

Deadlift
1) Warm-up
- 5–7 min easy cardio + hips/hamstrings/brace prep.
- Bar/RDL patterning x 8
- 40% x 5
- 55% x 3
- 65% x 2
- 75% x 1
- 82.5% x 1 (RPE ~7). If this feels ≥8, stop early and treat that as your top for the day.

2) Test ladder
- 87.5% x 1
- 92.5% x 1
- If RPE ≤8 and back position solid: 95% x 1
- Optional final: 97.5% x 1 only if 95% was clean with no hitching or rounding.

Example numbers from 170 kg pre-illness 1RM
- 82.5% 140 kg, 87.5% 149 kg, 92.5% 157 kg, 95% 162 kg, 97.5% 166 kg
- Likely landing: 155–165 kg clean single.

Back-off (optional)
- 2 x 1 @ 90% if fresh; otherwise move on.

Squat
- Keep this conservative since deadlift was tested first.

1) Warm-up
- Bar x 8–10
- 40% x 5
- 55% x 3
- 65% x 2
- 75% x 1
- 80–82.5% x 1

2) Test ladder (choose route based on feel)
- If 80–82.5% felt easy (≤RPE 7): 87.5% x 1, then 92.5% x 1. Only proceed to 95% if bar speed is still strong and technique pristine.
- If 80–82.5% felt moderate (RPE 7.5–8): take 87.5% x 1 and call it, or at most 90% x 1.

Example numbers from 140 kg pre-illness 1RM
- 80% 112 kg, 82.5% 116 kg, 87.5% 123 kg, 90% 126 kg, 92.5% 129 kg, 95% 133 kg
- Likely landing: 120–130 kg clean single.

Stop criteria
- Any rep shows loss of brace, knee cave you can’t correct, soft lockouts, hitching on deadlift, or RPE ≥9.5—stop the lift there.

Converting test outcomes to new training maxes
- Define e1RM using the best clean single: if you stop at a fast 92.5% single, you can extrapolate modestly, but we’ll be conservative.
- Training max (TM) for next mesocycle:
  - If you hit 95–100% clean at RPE ≤9: set TM = 97.5% of that best single.
  - If you hit 90–95% clean at RPE ≤9: set TM = 95% of that single (or use the single itself if you prefer).
  - If you only reached 85–90%: estimate e1RM from rep equations is noisy—set TM = that single or +2.5–5 kg maximum.
- Example: Bench best single 95 kg clean → TM = 92.5 kg. Squat best 127.5 kg clean → TM = 124 kg. Deadlift best 160 kg clean → TM = 156 kg.

Week 3 adjustments to accommodate testing
- Early-week sessions stay as planned but reduce accessory volume by 20–30% to keep freshness.
- Skip any AM run before test days. Keep the Week 3 long easy run 48+ hours away from the lower-body test.
- Post-test day: prioritize recovery (easy 15–20 min spin, mobility, high-carb meals, sleep 8+ h).

Optional: If you want a single-day test
- Do Bench first, then Squat, then Deadlift only to a strong 90–92.5% single. Higher cumulative fatigue will depress results, so use those numbers strictly as training max inputs, not true 1RMs.

This approach yields real, usable numbers while honoring recovery, so you can program Week 4+ with confidence.

Here’s a clean, week-by-week summary you can hand to the client. It includes working loads, rest guidance, and the return-to-running steps.

Week 1 — Reload and Movement Quality
- Lifts and loads (RPE ~6)
  - Squat: 4 x 5 at 87.5–90 kg (Conservative 85; if flying 92.5).
  - Bench: 4 x 5 at 62.5 kg (Conservative 60; if flying 65).
  - Deadlift: 3 x 4 at 110 kg (Conservative 105; if flying 112.5–115).
  - Accessories: RPE 6, 2–3 sets x 6–12 reps; stop well before grind.
- Running/cardio
  - 2 easy runs: 20–25 min and 25–30 min (conversational pace, RPE 3–4).
  - Optional GPP bike/row: 20–25 min instead of a third run.
- Rest days and spacing
  - 4 lift days: Lower, Upper, Full-body, GPP/Accessory.
  - Place Run A on the Upper day (separate by 6+ h or after lifting). Run B on a non-lifting day or 24+ h after Full-body.
  - 2 full rest or active-recovery days (walks/mobility only).

Week 2 — Small Intensity Bump, Build Volume
- Lifts and loads (top set RPE ~7; back-offs RPE 6–7)
  - Squat: 1 x 4 at ~70% ≈ 98 kg; then 3 x 5 at 65% ≈ 91 kg.
  - Bench: 1 x 4 at ~70% ≈ 70 kg; then 3 x 5 at 65% ≈ 65 kg.
  - Deadlift: 1 x 3 at ~70% ≈ 119 kg; then 3 x 3–4 at 65% ≈ 111 kg.
  - Accessories: Slightly heavier than Week 1, still submaximal.
- Running/cardio
  - 2 easy runs: 30–35 min and 35–40 min.
  - Optional strides after the longer run: 4 x 10 s relaxed with full walk-back.
  - Optional GPP bike/row: 25–30 min easy.
- Rest days and spacing
  - Keep 4 lift days. Put longer run 24+ h away from heavy lower-body work.
  - Maintain 1–2 true rest days (no intensity).

Week 3 — Readiness Check, Near-Return to Baseline + Testing
- Early week lifts (top exposures RPE 7–8; back-offs RPE 6–7)
  - Squat: Top 1 x 3 at 75–80% ≈ 105–112 kg; back-off 2–3 x 4 at 70% ≈ 98 kg.
  - Bench: Top 1 x 3 at 75–80% ≈ 75–80 kg; back-off 2–3 x 4 at 70% ≈ 70 kg.
  - Deadlift: Top 1 x 2–3 at 77–82% ≈ 131–139 kg; back-off 2–3 x 3 at 70% ≈ 119 kg.
- 1RM test (late Week 3; reduce accessories 20–30% to stay fresh)
  - Bench (mid-week): Work to clean single 90–97.5% (stop ≤RPE 9).
  - Deadlift then Squat (end-week): Deadlift to 92.5–97.5% clean single; Squat to 90–95% clean single if speed/form allow.
  - Set new training maxes from best clean singles (use ~95–97.5% of best as TM).
- Running/cardio
  - Run A: 35–40 min easy (+ 4–6 x 10 s strides if fresh).
  - Run B: 50–60 min easy to re-establish 10k duration (keep 48+ h away from lower-body test).
  - GPP: Very easy spin/walk 15–20 min on test week to prioritize recovery.
- Rest days and spacing
  - No runs before test days. Keep at least one full rest day before the lower-body test.
  - Ensure 1–2 true rest days this week.

Global guardrails and adjustments
- Auto-regulation: If any main-lift set creeps past RPE 7 in Weeks 1–2, drop 2.5–5 kg or cut a back-off set. In Week 3, do not exceed RPE 8 outside of testing.
- Recovery checks: Morning RHR within 10% of baseline, DOMS resolves in 24–36 h, easy runs feel easy. If not, hold or regress a week.
- Nutrition: Small daily surplus (+200–350 kcal), protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg, carbs 4–6 g/kg on lift+run days, fluids 35–45 ml/kg/day, creatine 3–5 g/day.
- Transition after testing: If singles were clean and recovery is normal, resume full-intensity work next mesocycle using new TMs; reintroduce RPE 8–9 top sets and normal weekly volume over 1–2 weeks.

Here’s a clean, week-by-week summary you can hand to the client. It includes working loads, rest guidance, and the return-to-running steps.

Week 1 — Reload and Movement Quality
- Lifts and loads (RPE ~6)
  - Squat: 4 x 5 at 87.5–90 kg (Conservative 85; if flying 92.5).
  - Bench: 4 x 5 at 62.5 kg (Conservative 60; if flying 65).
  - Deadlift: 3 x 4 at 110 kg (Conservative 105; if flying 112.5–115).
  - Accessories: RPE 6, 2–3 sets x 6–12 reps; stop well before grind.
- Running/cardio
  - 2 easy runs: 20–25 min and 25–30 min (conversational pace, RPE 3–4).
  - Optional GPP bike/row: 20–25 min instead of a third run.
- Rest days and spacing
  - 4 lift days: Lower, Upper, Full-body, GPP/Accessory.
  - Place Run A on the Upper day (separate by 6+ h or after lifting). Run B on a non-lifting day or 24+ h after Full-body.
  - 2 full rest or active-recovery days (walks/mobility only).

Week 2 — Small Intensity Bump, Build Volume
- Lifts and loads (top set RPE ~7; back-offs RPE 6–7)
  - Squat: 1 x 4 at ~70% ≈ 98 kg; then 3 x 5 at 65% ≈ 91 kg.
  - Bench: 1 x 4 at ~70% ≈ 70 kg; then 3 x 5 at 65% ≈ 65 kg.
  - Deadlift: 1 x 3 at ~70% ≈ 119 kg; then 3 x 3–4 at 65% ≈ 111 kg.
  - Accessories: Slightly heavier than Week 1, still submaximal.
- Running/cardio
  - 2 easy runs: 30–35 min and 35–40 min.
  - Optional strides after the longer run: 4 x 10 s relaxed with full walk-back.
  - Optional GPP bike/row: 25–30 min easy.
- Rest days and spacing
  - Keep 4 lift days. Put longer run 24+ h away from heavy lower-body work.
  - Maintain 1–2 true rest days (no intensity).

Week 3 — Readiness Check, Near-Return to Baseline + Testing
- Early week lifts (top exposures RPE 7–8; back-offs RPE 6–7)
  - Squat: Top 1 x 3 at 75–80% ≈ 105–112 kg; back-off 2–3 x 4 at 70% ≈ 98 kg.
  - Bench: Top 1 x 3 at 75–80% ≈ 75–80 kg; back-off 2–3 x 4 at 70% ≈ 70 kg.
  - Deadlift: Top 1 x 2–3 at 77–82% ≈ 131–139 kg; back-off 2–3 x 3 at 70% ≈ 119 kg.
- 1RM test (late Week 3; reduce accessories 20–30% to stay fresh)
  - Bench (mid-week): Work to clean single 90–97.5% (stop ≤RPE 9).
  - Deadlift then Squat (end-week): Deadlift to 92.5–97.5% clean single; Squat to 90–95% clean single if speed/form allow.
  - Set new training maxes from best clean singles (use ~95–97.5% of best as TM).
- Running/cardio
  - Run A: 35–40 min easy (+ 4–6 x 10 s strides if fresh).
  - Run B: 50–60 min easy to re-establish 10k duration (keep 48+ h away from lower-body test).
  - GPP: Very easy spin/walk 15–20 min on test week to prioritize recovery.
- Rest days and spacing
  - No runs before test days. Keep at least one full rest day before the lower-body test.
  - Ensure 1–2 true rest days this week.

Global guardrails and adjustments
- Auto-regulation: If any main-lift set creeps past RPE 7 in Weeks 1–2, drop 2.5–5 kg or cut a back-off set. In Week 3, do not exceed RPE 8 outside of testing.
- Recovery checks: Morning RHR within 10% of baseline, DOMS resolves in 24–36 h, easy runs feel easy. If not, hold or regress a week.
- Nutrition: Small daily surplus (+200–350 kcal), protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg, carbs 4–6 g/kg on lift+run days, fluids 35–45 ml/kg/day, creatine 3–5 g/day.
- Transition after testing: If singles were clean and recovery is normal, resume full-intensity work next mesocycle using new TMs; reintroduce RPE 8–9 top sets and normal weekly volume over 1–2 weeks.
